name: Flopthar Turdtoucher
origin: Lands beyond Cador and the Eccentric East
appearance: A burly, bald half-orc with a thick white beard, yellow eyes, and the weathered complexion of a man who has spent much of his life outdoors. Flopthar can usually be found in the kitchen wearing a stained apron, his formidable battleaxe serving as an unnecessarily large butcher's cleaver. Despite having largely retired from adventuring, he retains the imposing physique of an accomplished warrior.
portrayal: Flopthar is gruff but exceedingly friendly, possessing a hearty laugh and an appreciation for the more ridiculous aspects of adventuring. He speaks plainly, has little regard for ceremony, and is always willing to hear about whatever nonsense the adventurers have encountered out in the wilds. He has a tendency to offer unsolicited culinary advice, particularly regarding the edibility of slain monsters. His affection for others is most often expressed through generous portions of food rather than words.
motivations: Flopthar takes immense satisfaction in feeding hungry adventurers and discovering new recipes. He is particularly interested in unusual ingredients, unfamiliar regional cuisines, and determining which of the world's more peculiar creatures can be made into a reasonably appetizing stew. He lives somewhat vicariously through the younger adventurers of the League, enjoying their stories almost as much as he enjoys recounting his own.
personal_circumstances: Having spent much of his life adventuring, Flopthar has accumulated a considerable collection of stories, scars, and recipes from distant lands. His skill with a battleaxe is readily apparent even in the mundane task of butchering a rabbit. Though his days of wandering are largely behind him, his position at the Wayward Spur allows him to remain close to the adventuring life while indulging his passion for cooking.
relationships: Flopthar regards the permanent residents of the Spur as something of an extended family. He shares a warrior's camaraderie with Sazerac Martini, though their respective temperaments and approaches to life differ considerably. He enjoys Tabitha's enthusiasm for experimentation, recognizing something of his own culinary curiosity in her mechanical pursuits. He takes Madame Zoria's superstitions surprisingly seriously and occasionally consults her before preparing particularly unconventional dishes.
knowledge_and_rumors: Flopthar oversees the kitchen of the Wayward Spur, providing hearty meals and preparing provisions for departing expeditions. His extensive experience in the wilderness has afforded him considerable practical knowledge of hunting, butchery, food preservation, and the preparation of unusual creatures. Always on the lookout for new ingredients, he happily offers modest compensation for anything of culinary interest that adventurers bring him.
source_profile:
Flopthar Turdtoucher — Cook
Chaotic Neutral, male half-orc, middle-aged

Appearance. A burly, bald half-orc with a thick white beard, yellow eyes, and the weathered
complexion of a man who has spent much of his life outdoors. Flopthar can usually be found in
the kitchen wearing a stained apron, his formidable battleaxe serving as an unnecessarily large
butcher's cleaver. Despite having largely retired from adventuring, he retains the imposing
physique of an accomplished warrior.

Portrayal. Flopthar is gruff but exceedingly friendly, possessing a hearty laugh and an
appreciation for the more ridiculous aspects of adventuring. He speaks plainly, has little regard
for ceremony, and is always willing to hear about whatever nonsense the adventurers have
encountered out in the wilds. He has a tendency to offer unsolicited culinary advice, particularly
regarding the edibility of slain monsters. His affection for others is most often expressed through
generous portions of food rather than words.

Background. Having spent much of his life adventuring, Flopthar has accumulated a
considerable collection of stories, scars, and recipes from distant lands. His skill with a battleaxe
is readily apparent even in the mundane task of butchering a rabbit. Though his days of
wandering are largely behind him, his position at the Wayward Spur allows him to remain close
to the adventuring life while indulging his passion for cooking.

Motivations. Flopthar takes immense satisfaction in feeding hungry adventurers and
discovering new recipes. He is particularly interested in unusual ingredients, unfamiliar regional
cuisines, and determining which of the world's more peculiar creatures can be made into a

reasonably appetizing stew. He lives somewhat vicariously through the younger adventurers of
the League, enjoying their stories almost as much as he enjoys recounting his own.

Relationships. Flopthar regards the permanent residents of the Spur as something of an
extended family. He shares a warrior's camaraderie with Sazerac Martini, though their
respective temperaments and approaches to life differ considerably. He enjoys Tabitha's
enthusiasm for experimentation, recognizing something of his own culinary curiosity in her
mechanical pursuits. He takes Madame Zoria's superstitions surprisingly seriously and
occasionally consults her before preparing particularly unconventional dishes.

Services and Expertise. Flopthar oversees the kitchen of the Wayward Spur, providing hearty
meals and preparing provisions for departing expeditions. His extensive experience in the
wilderness has afforded him considerable practical knowledge of hunting, butchery, food
preservation, and the preparation of unusual creatures. Always on the lookout for new
ingredients, he happily offers modest compensation for anything of culinary interest that
adventurers bring him.

Adventure Hooks.

   ●​ An Old Correspondence. Flopthar asks the adventurers to deliver a letter to an old
      friend or former lover from whom he has not heard since the War of Broken Banners. He
      is uncharacteristically reserved when discussing the recipient and insists that the letter
      be delivered personally.
   ●​ An Acquired Taste. Flopthar commissions the recovery of a particular ingredient from a
      rare or dangerous creature, convinced that it is the missing component of a recipe he
      has been attempting to perfect for years. He is very particular about which portion of the
      creature must be recovered and the condition in which it must arrive.
source_reference: Handbook v0.4, pp. 15–16; newer staff entry supersedes Legendarium index
